research_question: In women at risk of preterm birth, does antenatal magnesium sulphate given for fetal neuroprotection, compared with placebo, reduce cerebral palsy in their children assessed at about 18 months to 2 years' corrected age?
outcome_description: Number of children diagnosed with cerebral palsy (trial's own diagnosis, e.g. abnormalities of tone with loss of motor function, or an overall neurological diagnosis by a paediatric assessor) out of the number of children assessed/counted in each arm at the first follow-up reported between 18 months and 2 years' corrected age. Denominator is the paper's own denominator for this outcome (children with data on cerebral palsy preferred; otherwise surviving children assessed, live births with data, or number randomised, stated as such). Children are counted, not mothers or pregnancies; multiple magnesium dose regimens are combined into one magnesium group with the placebo group used once. School-age follow-up is not used.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR below 1) means fewer children developed cerebral palsy after antenatal magnesium sulphate than after placebo, i.e. the result favours magnesium sulphate.
search_queries: antenatal magnesium sulphate neuroprotection preterm birth cerebral palsy randomised trial
magnesium sulfate fetal neuroprotection placebo-controlled trial preterm infant outcome 2 years
magnesium sulphate before preterm birth cerebral palsy children follow-up controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised placebo-controlled trial of antenatal magnesium sulphate given to women at risk of preterm birth with a neuroprotective intent
Reports childhood neurodevelopmental follow-up including cerebral palsy at roughly 18 months to 2 years' corrected age
Reports quantitative data allowing extraction of cerebral palsy events and totals per arm (counts, proportions, or percentages convertible to counts)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between antenatal magnesium sulphate and a placebo control (e.g. comparison of two magnesium regimens, magnesium versus another active drug, or magnesium given solely for pre-eclampsia/eclampsia or tocolysis without placebo neuroprotection comparison)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no events/totals, proportions, means+SDs, t/F values, or odds/risk ratios)
Completely unrelated to antenatal magnesium sulphate and child neurological outcome after preterm birth
moderators_to_extract: Gestational age at randomisation (threshold for eligibility)
Total magnesium sulphate dose regimen (loading dose with/without maintenance infusion)
Indication for treatment (imminent preterm birth, preterm prelabour rupture of membranes, fetal growth restriction)
Timing/age at follow-up assessment (months corrected age)
Denominator type used (children with CP data, surviving children assessed, live births, or randomised)
Risk of bias / loss to follow-up rate
Sample size category (number of children assessed)
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio (magnesium ÷ placebo) using a fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model where available, otherwise random effects. RR < 1 favours magnesium sulphate. Do not pool death, death or cerebral palsy combined, substantial gross motor dysfunction, blindness, deafness, maternal outcomes, or adverse events.
